headline: Approved Chippanee golf course fund and $99,750 workers' compensation contract; recommended $1,250,000 and $689,545 budget transfers to Joint Meeting.
summary: Most items passed on a consent agenda, including a bid waiver for security cameras at three City parking garages. A $50,000 transfer for Police repairs and maintenance was recommended after the mayor said repair prices rose and accidents involving City vehicles increased. The meeting also heard a Board of Education budget update reporting Private Outplaced tuitions $1.4 million over budget.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda by voice vote with no opposition, and recommended its budget items to a Joint Meeting of the City Council and Board of Finance.
Recommended a $50,000 transfer from the General Fund Contingency account to Police repairs and maintenance, by voice vote with no opposition.
Recommended a $49,745 transfer within the Equipment Building Sinking Fund, by voice vote with no opposition.
Approved a bid waiver to Marcus Communications for installing security cameras at the three City parking garages, by voice vote with no opposition.

Approved the award of the workers' compensation claims administration and risk management contract to Omni Underwriting Managers LLC dba FutureComp at $99,750 annually, by voice vote with no opposition.
Recommended a $40,000 transfer from the General Fund Contingency account for professional fees, by voice vote with no opposition.
Approved a bid waiver to Culpepper RFP for the RFP advisor fee for the pension consultant, by voice vote with no opposition.
Recommended a $689,545 additional appropriation within the General Fund as of June 30, 2026, by voice vote with no opposition.
Recommended a $1,250,000 transfer from the General Fund Contingency account as of June 30, 2026, by voice vote with no opposition.
Recommended a $101,021 additional appropriation and $7,995 in transfers within the Road Improvements Fund, by voice vote with no opposition.
Approved creating Fund 410 for the Chippanee Municipal Golf Course, by voice vote with no opposition.

Board of Finance Minutes 
 
 
Commissioner O’Brien made a motion seconded by Commissioner Massarelli 
 
“To approve the consent agenda and to recommend approval of this action to a Joint Meeting of the 
City Council and Board of Finance.” 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried 
 
 
4. Police Department: 
a. Transfer of $50,000 from the General Fund Contingency account  
 
Mayor Ellen Zoppo Sassu made a motion seconded by Commissioner Mace 
 
“To transfer $50,000 from the General Fund Contingency account to Police – Repairs & 
Maintenance and to recommend approval of this action to a Joint Meeting of the City Council and 
Board of Finance.” 
 
Mayor Zoppo Sassu stated the new vendor that received the bid has increased the price of the repairs, 
and there have been an increase in accidents involving City vehicles.  
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
5. Public Works: 
a. Transfer of $49,745 within the Equipment Building Sinking Fund 
 
 
Commissioner Peterson made a motion seconded by Commissioner Massarelli  
 
“To transfer $49,745 within the Equipment Building Sinking Fund and to recommend approval of 
this action to a Joint Meeting of the City Council and Board of Finance.” 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
b. Approval of a bid waiver to Marcus Communications  
 
 
Commissioner Peterson made a motion seconded by Commissioner Mace 
 
“To approve a bid waiver to Marcus Communications for the installation of security cameras at the 
three City parking garages.” 
 
Raymond Rogozinski stated Public Works reached out to a few vendors, compatible with existing 
system, as there were issues in the past when going out to bid for security systems and would like to 
stay with the existing vendor. 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.
October 27, 2026 
Board of Finance Minutes 
 
 
6. Purchasing: 
a. Award the Worker’s Compensation Claims Administration and Risk Management 
Services to Omni Underwriting Managers LLC dba FutureComp 
 
Commissioner Campion made a motion seconded by Commissioner O’Brien 
 
“To award Contract 2P27-007 Worker’s Compensation Claims Administration and Risk 
Management Services to Omni Underwriting Managers LLC dba FutureComp in the amount of 
$99,750 annually.” 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
7. Board of Education:   
a. Budget Update 
 
Jodi Bond gave the budget update from the Board of Education as of September 30, 2026.  Actual 
expenditures total $23,815,860 and encumbrances total $97,930,091 through 9/30/26, leaving an 
available balance of $27,079,935.  While the overall Special Education budget is still below budget, 
the Private Outplaced tuitions line is overbudget by $1.4 million.  
 
Pending August & September Federal and State reimbursement, the Café snapshot reflects a surplus 
of $721,972. This surplus will be fully expended in FY27. 49,842 breakfasts and 119,469 lunches were 
served in September. 
 
The food steamers at both BCHS and BEHS recently broke and had to be replaced.  The costs were:  
$41,128.86 at BE (convection steamer) and $51,008.45 (pressure steamer) at BC. Both of the steamers 
are over 40 years old; they have both had the boiler part of the steamer unit replaced about 12 
years ago.  The steamers are used on almost a daily basis. They are used to cook a wide variety of 
items: taco meat or other types of diced or cut up meats, rice, macaroni and cheese, all of the 
vegetables, sauces and gravy’s, reheating of already cooked food and the steam kettle is used for 
soups, mashed potatoes, chili and boiled water when needed. They are a vital component of a kitchen 
of this size and it has been difficult to operate without them since they have been down. 
 
As of October 1, 2026, 1,770 of the 7,806 enrolled Bristol students are identified as requiring Special 
Education programming. This enrollment reflects 22.67% of the total BPS student population. As of 
October 1, 129 students with disabilities required out-of-district placements at private special 
education school programs. There were 87 students requiring special education programming services 
at other public out-of-district schools, including magnet schools. 
 
During the month of September 2026 41% (24 of 56) of the newly registered students were identified 
as students with special education programming needs at the time of registration with 2 of the newly 
registered students required programming and services at an out-of-district special education school 
program. During the month of September, there were 24 211 and 8 911 calls. 
 
Chairman Maikowski requested Dr Martino compare our trends or other school districts to see if they 
are similar for year by year, to see if everyone is having the same problem.
October 27, 2026 
Board of Finance Minutes 
 
 
 
8. Comptroller’s Office: 
a. Transfer of $40,000 from the General Fund Contingency account  
 
Commissioner Massarelli made a motion seconded by Commissioner Campion 
 
“To transfer $40,000 from the General Fund Contingency account for Professional Fees and to 
recommend approval of this action to a Joint Meeting of the City Council and Board of Finance.” 
 
Chairman Maikowski stated the City will be going out to RFP for the Pension Advisor and this 
request is to engage a consultant to assist with the RFP process.  
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
b. Approval of a bid waiver to Culpepper RFP 
 
Commissioner Massarelli made a motion seconded by Commissioner Campion 
 
“To approve a bid waiver to Culpepper RFP for the RFP Advisor Fee for the pension consultant.” 
 
Chairman Maikowski asked Diane to review the process, Diane explained two firms were reviewed 
Culpepper and USI (formerly Hooker and Holcombe). Culpepper specializes in RFP processes for 
pension advisor services and has Connecticut based clients.    
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
c. Additional appropriation of $689,545 within the General Fund as of June 30, 2026 
 
Commissioner O’Brien made a motion seconded by Commissioner Mace 
 
“To make an additional appropriation of $689,545 within the General Fund as of June 30, 2026 and 
to recommend approval of this action to a Joint Meeting of the City Council and Board of Finance.” 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
d. Transfer of $1,250,000 from the General Fund Contingency account as of June 30, 
2026 
 
Commissioner O’Brien made a motion seconded by Commissioner Mace 
 
“To Transfer of $1,250,000 from the General Fund Contingency account within the General Fund as 
of June 30, 2026 and to recommend approval of this action to a Joint Meeting of the City Council 
and Board of Finance.” 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.
October 27, 2026 
Board of Finance Minutes 
 
 
e. Additional appropriation of $101,021 and transfers totaling $7,995 within the Road 
Improvements Fund as of June 30, 2026 
 
Commissioner Mace made a motion seconded by Commissioner Massarelli 
 
“To make an additional appropriation of $101,021 and transfers totaling $7,995 within the Road 
Improvements Fund as of June 30, 2026 and to recommend approval of this action to a Joint Meeting 
of the City Council and Board of Finance.” 
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.  
 
f. Create Fund 410 - Chippanee Municipal Golf Course Fund 
 
Commissioner Mace made a motion seconded by Commissioner O’Brien 
 
“To create Fund 410 - Chippanee Municipal Golf Course Fund” 
 
Diane Waldron stated there will be an action item at a future meeting to establish the line items and 
allocate the $500,0000, but this will get the fund set up as well as allocate funding for initial operating 
costs.   
 
Following a voice vote in which there was no opposition, the Chairperson declared the motion 
carried.

Mark
